subject.title: Feature Request: Add channel creation to message tool

question: Should OpenClaw expose agent-driven Slack and Discord channel creation through the message tool, and what explicit action gate, scope, requester, and approval boundary must guard it?
rationale: The implementation shape is clear, but creating channels mutates workspace/server structure and adds at least one Slack config/default surface, so automation should not choose the authority model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve gated provider-owned implementation
options.body: Add Slack channel creation behind an explicit Slack channel-management action gate and setup-scope/docs updates, and land Discord CLI parity only once the existing Discord gate is accepted for local CLI use.

options.title: Limit to Discord parity first
options.body: Keep this issue open for broader Slack/provider design and let the existing Discord CLI PR or a replacement cover only the current Discord runtime gap.

options.title: Keep channel provisioning external
options.body: Do not expose channel creation through the message tool yet; document direct Slack/Discord admin APIs or manual provisioning as the supported path until a stronger security model exists.

recommendation.title: Approve gated provider-owned implementation
recommendation.body: Add Slack channel creation behind an explicit Slack channel-management action gate and setup-scope/docs updates, and land Discord CLI parity only once the existing Discord gate is accepted for local CLI use.

likelyOwner.reason: The history and prior issue discussion point to steipete as the strongest current routing candidate across message CLI, Slack actions, Discord action gates, and the prior review context.
